tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Diagnose...Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms (slow, erroring, unreachable, can't scale) rather than internal mechanics, explicitly lists many trigger contexts including cases where the user doesn't name the domain directly (e.g., 'even if they do not mention FailureReason, port 8080...'), and routes out of scope to other skills. It is a dense paragraph but remains within reasonable length for the complexity of the domain.
tests.evidence: Diagnose an Amazon SageMaker real-time inference endpoint that fails, errors, cannot be reached or is slow. Use this skill when creating or updating an endpoint fails or leaves it Failed...even if they do not mention FailureReason, port 8080, VPC endpoints, security groups, data capture or scaling policies by name.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is entirely domain-specific — check-ids, APIs, metrics, guardrails — with no generic explanations of what SageMaker or CloudWatch are. It is dense but every sentence conveys project-specific knowledge the agent wouldn't otherwise have.
tests.evidence: "A variant can be `InService` with `CurrentInstanceCount` = 0 (scaled in, scale-to-zero, or a leftover)."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The check catalog table is a concise index (what-it-catches), not the full detection rules/remediations/citations, which the body explicitly says live in the reference file. No large reference data blocks or detailed conditional-branch content appear inline.
tests.evidence: "The full six-column detection rules, remediations, and citations live in the reference — the table below is a what-it-catches index."

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All six references/ files are linked via markdown links in the body (checks-sagemaker-inference-endpoints.md, collection-reference.md, cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md, api-quirks.md, metrics-and-logs.md, known-causes.md).

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is paired with a specific triggering condition for when to load it, both in the Router table and elsewhere.
tests.evidence: "Load [known-causes.md](references/known-causes.md) whenever the user names an error or symptom; match it to a section..."

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (guardrails, review procedure steps, severity rules) are given exact prescriptive instructions, while diagnostic reasoning (matching symptoms, assembling findings) explains the why, giving the agent latitude to apply judgment within bounds.
tests.evidence: "Never call `UpdateEndpoint`, ... or any other mutating API." vs. "Match the symptom, confirm with the collection calls, then report with the check-id and severity from the catalog."

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present multiple competing tools for the same task; each diagnostic step specifies a clear single API/metric to use, with no equal-option menus.
tests.evidence: Router table entries each specify one 'First read' API per symptom, e.g. "application-autoscaling:DescribeScalableTargets for the variant" — no competing alternatives are listed as equal options.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable diagnostic procedure (Review Procedure steps, Router matching, check catalog) applicable to any endpoint/symptom, not a one-off instance; specific items (templates, check-ids) are details within that reusable approach.
tests.evidence: "Run the steps in order and track progress against this checklist. Each step depends on state gathered by the one before it."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has a dedicated 'Common wrong answers' and 'Error Handling' section documenting concrete, non-obvious pitfalls (InService≠serving, empty scalable targets≠off, no datapoints≠zero) that the agent would otherwise get wrong.
tests.evidence: "The endpoint is `InService`, so it's serving traffic." ... "Confirm a non-zero instance count and recent `Invocations` before calling it healthy"

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces structured health reports and an explicit template is provided in assets/, linked in the body for use when a full report is requested.
tests.evidence: "When a full report is requested, the output follows [endpoint-health-report-template.md](assets/endpoint-health-report-template.md)."

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline output template exists in the body; the report template is stored in assets/ and referenced conditionally rather than embedded.
tests.evidence: Body only references "[endpoint-health-report-template.md](assets/endpoint-health-report-template.md)" — the template itself does not appear in the body.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file is explicitly linked in multiple places in the body.
tests.evidence: "[endpoint-health-report-template.md](assets/endpoint-health-report-template.md) — load when a full report is requested"

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset link specifies the exact condition for loading it (when a full report is requested).
tests.evidence: "load when a full report is requested: endpoint report format (per-endpoint state, findings with check-ids and severities...)"

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset reference uses a relative path from the skill root with no traversal or absolute paths.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The Review Procedure is presented as an ordered checkbox checklist with 'Step N:' labels, and the detailed elaboration section explicitly references 'Step 5' by name, matching the required format.
tests.evidence: "- [ ] Step 1: Enumerate endpoints and resolve their real state." ... "### Step 5 detail: the two-namespace rule"

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit self-validation gate before presenting output, checking check-id accuracy, observed-vs-inferred values, namespace coverage, severity correctness, and guardrail compliance.
tests.evidence: "Before presenting, re-check your output against this list. Treat it as a gate, not a suggestion."
